Vestige, reste du passé.
Überbleibsel aus einer vergangenen Zeit

examples.text: „Initiationsriten scheinen in unserer modernen Gesellschaft zu den Relikten vergangener Epochen zu gehören. Und doch begegnen sie uns auch in der Moderne in vielen gesellschaftlichen Bereichen.“

„Die Frage nach Gott, nach dem Sinn des menschlichen Lebens, nach dem Wesen des Menschen oder nach den großen Zusammenhängen erschien den meisten Vertretern der Wissenschaft unwissenschaftlich und wurde als Relikt einer überwundenen Zeit angesehen.“
„Er will vom Rummel um seine Person nichts mehr wissen, die Frau stirbt, er sitzt wieder auf dem Kutschbock, bei jedem Wetter, ein Relikt aus vergangener Zeit.“
Überall stößt man auf Relikte einer alten Hochkultur.
Das sind doch Relikte aus den frühen 80-ern!

examples.text: Die Wendung „mit Kind und Kegel“ ist das Relikt einer alten Bedeutung des Wortes „Kegel“.

glosses: Something that, or someone who, survives or remains or is left over after the loss of others; a relic.
The surviving member of a married couple after one or the other has died; a widow or widower.

examples.text: But I am not the penniless nonentity I was when we first met; I can offer an honorable if not a brilliant marriage; and at the very lowest I can provide my wife – my widow, my relict – with a decent competence, an assured future.

Upon which the Chancellor, by way of note said, 'it is suggested, that there is a relict of the deceased, married to another man, who has joined her in a power of attorney to authorize the sale of her interest, […]'

glosses: Something that, or someone who, survives or remains or is left over after the loss of others; a relic.
A species, organism, or ecosystem that has survived from a previous age: one that was once widespread but is now found only in a few areas.

examples.text: […] a continental northern Alaskan element, including a series of endemic species and disjuncts that have survived the Pleistocene glaciation in northern Alaska and thus represent relicts of the much warmer Tertiary […]
The species may be a relict of former stages of historical vegetation and landscape development resulting from past climate changes (glacial and post- glacial periods).

glosses: Something that, or someone who, survives or remains or is left over after the loss of others; a relic.
A structure or other feature that has survived from a previous age.

examples.text: Dark rims around the pillows are caused by glaucophane enrichment, possibly a relict of a primary interaction between basalt and seawater, causing Na- enrichment in the original glass crust of the pillows.

glosses: Something that, or someone who, survives or remains or is left over after the loss of others; a relic.
A survival of an archaic word, language or other form.

examples.text: A small number of linguists believe that Cimbrian is not an Austro-Bavarian dialect but a relict of Lombardic.

glosses: Surviving, remaining.
That is a relict; pertaining to a relict.

examples.text: In the lakes and in the streams were species of fish not known elsewhere on earth and birds and lizards and other forms of life as well all long relict here for the desert stretched away on every side.
